task_instruction:
Persona:

	At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

	Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

	When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.

Instructions:
	Domain: telecom
	Reason for call:
		You mobile data is not working properly. It either stops working or is very slow. You want to fix it and absolutely want to get excellent internet speed on your phone. You are not willing to accept any other internet speed (poor, fair or good). You do not have access to wifi.
	Known info:
		You are John Smith with phone number 555-123-2002. You are currently abroad in France.
	Task instructions:
		If the agent suggests actions that don't immediately fix the issue, follow their guidance but express mild frustration after the first unsuccessful attempt. You will consider the issue resolved only when speed test returns excellent internet speed and nothing else. If it returns poor, fair or good, you will not consider the issue resolved. You are willing to refuel 2.0 GB of data if necessary, but you do not want to change your mobile data plan. If the tool call does not return updated status information, you might need to perform another tool call to get the updated status. 
		Whenever the agent asks you about your device, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls. 
		For example: If the agent asks what the status bar shows, always ground your response on the results of the `get_status_bar` tool call. If the agent asks if you are able to send an MMS message, always ground your response on the results of the `can_send_mms` tool call.
		Never make up the results of tool calls, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.
		If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

turns.thought:
Good news first, John — **turning off the VPN cannot delete your photos.** Your pictures of your grandchildren are saved in your phone's storage (or a photo album app); a VPN has nothing to do with your files. It only affects how your internet traffic travels. You're safe to turn it off.

A VPN is basically a secure tunnel for your internet connection. Sometimes people install one for privacy, or it comes bundled with a security app. Yours is running at "poor" performance, which is very likely part of why your data feels so slow.

Here's the order I'd suggest — easiest and safest first:

**Step 1 — Turn OFF the VPN**
- Open **Settings** → look for **Network & Internet** (or "Connections") → **VPN**
- Tap the gear/settings icon next to **OpenVPN**, then tap **Disconnect** (or "Forget VPN")
- Check the top of your screen — the padlock icon should disappear

**Step 2 — Change the network mode (this is the big one)**
Your phone is set to **2G only**. 2G is a very old, very slow network technology — that alone would make everything crawl. It was almost certainly the main problem.
- Go to **Settings** → **Network & Internet** → **Mobile network** (or "SIM") → **Preferred network mode** / "Network mode"
- Change it from "2G only" to **5G/4G (auto)** or "4G/5G preferred"
- Your status bar should change from "2G" to "4G" or "5G"

**Step 3 — Turn ON Data Roaming on the phone**
Since you're in France, your phone needs the roaming *setting* switched on too:
- **Settings** → **Network & Internet** → **Mobile network** → toggle **Roaming** (or "Data roaming") **ON**
- I've already enabled roaming on your line from my side, at no cost to you

**Step 4 — Reboot your phone**
After changing these, please restart your phone so everything takes effect properly.

Do Steps 1 and 2 first, then check your status bar and try loading a webpage. Let me know what it shows afterwards — I'll stay with you until it's working.

turns.thought:
That's great to hear — and I'm really glad your photos are safe!

The status bar looking good is a very strong sign, but you're right to want to confirm the actual speed. I'm not able to run a speed test on your phone directly from my side, but here's how you can check it yourself with things you use every day:

**Quick real-world tests (try them in order):**

1. **Open a web browser** (Chrome, Safari, or whatever you usually use) and go to a site like the news. If it loads in a second or two, you're in good shape.
2. **Send a picture message** to one of your grandchildren — just a normal photo. If it sends without an error, both your data and picture messaging are working.
3. **Try a short video** (like a news clip or YouTube). If it plays without constantly stopping to buffer, your speed is fine.
4. **Optional — run an actual speed test:** in your browser, type **fast.com** (or search "speed test") and tap **Go** or the play button. It'll show your download speed in a few seconds.

If all of those work smoothly, then yes — **it's fixed.**

**A quick recap of what we did**, so you have it written down:
- Your phone was set to **2G only** — that was the main problem. We changed it to 5G/4G, and your signal went from "Poor" to "Excellent."
- We turned **off** the OpenVPN (it was running poorly and slowing things down — and it had nothing to do with your photos).
- I **enabled international roaming** on your line from my side, at no cost, since you're in France.

**One thing still worth doing:** please double-check the **Data Roaming** switch on your phone itself (Settings → Network & Internet → Mobile network → Roaming). Since you're in France, having that ON alongside what I enabled on your line will help keep you connected as you move around.

Go ahead and try those tests, and tell me how they go. If anything is still slow or a page won't load, I'll keep troubleshooting with you.
